title: arm-benefit-net: treatment-conditioned deep learning on public oncology clinical-trial transcriptomics
description: PyTorch framework and reproducible analysis asking whether pre-treatment tumour transcriptomes can identify which trial arm benefits which patient. ArmNet, a multi-task network with a shared tumour representation and one head per arm, is benchmarked against clinical, ridge, gradient-boosting and pooled neural-network models under nested, patient-level cross-validation on 741 randomised HER2-negative patients from the I-SPY2 platform trial (GEO GSE194040). Benefit is evaluated with randomisation-based interaction tests, c-for-benefit and inverse-probability-weighted policy value. Explanations use Integrated Gradients, and transfer is tested in the IMvigor210 atezolizumab cohort together with a deep Cox survival model and BulkFormer foundation-model embeddings. Includes a Nature-style report (docs/report.md) and an 11-lesson hands-on PyTorch course (lessons/). Main finding: expression improves prediction of pathologic complete response (AUC 0.765 vs 0.723 for clinical subtype), but no model identifies arm-specific benefit beyond subtype at single-trial scale. Developed with an AI coding agent (Claude Code); every step was reviewed and tested.
